set.request: Approve / Improve on any page: ext/Ask's floating ? gains Approve/Improve keyed by the page's own url in the shared verdicts.jsonl; the approved layouts page gains a live library of every approved url; mount() on ten named layout pages; headless proof; docs.
steps: read the brief, ext/Ask (Ask.js, pick.js, chat.js, reply.js), browse/verdicts.js and browse/page.js, the approved page, the layout skill
build verdict.js: verdict_mark() / verdict_acts(), sharing browse's verdicts.jsonl keyed by page url (never a browse id) — say why they can't collide
wire verdict_mark/verdict_acts into chat.js's mount(), gated on available() (which turned out to already BE the new edit() switch, landed mid-task)
mount() on the ten named pages: practice/catalog, practice/reader, practice/workbench, shell, labs/blogx, labs/decks, labs/mag, labs/screens, labs/sections, labs/shells
the approved page's live library — adapt to its mid-task move from imagine/design/layout/approved/ to layouts/doc/studies/approved/
headless proof on PORT 8137: console-error crawl, the real approve/verify/cleanup round trip, fix the isConnected race the proof caught
docs: ext/Ask readme + decisions.md, the approved page's own decisions.md, the layout skill clause
set.outcome: **Approve/Improve now lives on any page, not just browse's 102 catalogued items.** `ext/Ask`'s floating `?` (`mount({ app, url })`) gains the check/pen mark plus Approve/Improve buttons — `verdict.js` — writing one line to the SAME `/layouts/verdicts.jsonl` `/layouts/browse/` already reads and writes, keyed by the page's own url so it can never collide with a browse catalogue id (0 of 102 ids contain a `/`; every url does). Mounted on ten layout pages: [`/layouts/practice/catalog/`](/layouts/practice/catalog/), [`/layouts/practice/reader/`](/layouts/practice/reader/), [`/layouts/practice/workbench/`](/layouts/practice/workbench/), [`/layouts/shell/`](/layouts/shell/), [`/layouts/labs/blogx/`](/layouts/labs/blogx/), [`/layouts/labs/decks/`](/layouts/labs/decks/), [`/layouts/labs/mag/`](/layouts/labs/mag/), [`/layouts/labs/screens/`](/layouts/labs/screens/), [`/layouts/labs/sections/`](/layouts/labs/sections/), [`/layouts/labs/shells/`](/layouts/labs/shells/) — plus the module's own demo page, [`/framework/ext/Ask/`](/framework/ext/Ask/), which now carries a real Approve/Improve on itself. The approved layouts page — moved mid-task by a sibling minion to [`/layouts/doc/studies/approved/`](/layouts/doc/studies/approved/) — gained a live **library** section: every url whose newest verdict is Approve, as a picture card when `/layouts/browse/` has a screenshot for it, a title link otherwise. Proved headless on a private server (PORT 8137): zero console errors at 400/1280/3440 on three of the ten pages (workbench, shell — its own `render()` — and mag — its own `column()`); a real Approve on `/layouts/practice/workbench/` showed the check mark on the control within seconds, then the same test caught a genuine bug — the approved library's first draw silently skipped rendering because of a stray `isConnected` guard copied from the wrong place in browse's own pattern — fixed and re-proved (now shows the linked card), and the guard turned out to have the identical bug already latent in `verdict_mark()`/`verdict_acts()` themselves, fixed there too before anyone had a chance to hit it live. The test verdict was then deleted from `verdicts.jsonl` (the owner is the only real writer) and the private server killed by its exact PID. Docs: [`ext/Ask/readme.md`](/framework/ext/Ask/readme.md), [`ext/Ask/doc/decisions.md`](/framework/ext/Ask/doc/decisions.md) (the full record — the shared-file decision, the `location.pathname`/`router.active` trap this caught before it ever shipped, the `isConnected` trap, the optional `reply()` integration), [`/layouts/doc/studies/approved/doc/decisions.md`](/layouts/doc/studies/approved/doc/decisions.md) (the mid-task move, the library's own design), one clause in the layout skill's closed-set bullet (also fixed its now-stale link). **Left, on purpose:** a page's own `?` and browse's wall card for the SAME page carry two separate verdict trails (different keys, by design — proved empirically: approving via the `?` does not mark the browse card) — the owner's call if these should ever merge; the seven pages beyond the three proof pages share the identical `content()` mount pattern already proven clean rather than each getting its own crawl; `verdict_acts()`'s optional `m`/`reply()` path has no live caller yet (no mounted page owns a task log) — ready for a task-detail page to pass `m` directly; `css-scopes.txt`'s `ask-` line is still unregistered, a pre-existing open item (`ext/Ask/doc/decisions.md`) that now also covers `verdict.js`'s classes, outside this task's write fence.
